eps.d: Tom Howard, along with son Leo and daughter Lynne, celebrate their success in the prestigious Commadore Cup but when Tom reveals he has been made redundant from Southern Aviation, none of his family is too happy. Jack Rolf is concerned that his business, The Mermaid Boat Yard, is about to go bankrupt.

Ken Masters is interested in taking over the Mermaid Yard. He employs Leo Howard at the local pertol station and is eager to employ Jan. Meanwhile, Jan and Tom argue incessantly about how he should spend his redundancy money. Polly Urquhart's daughter Abby returns from finishing school but she has not turned out how the Urquhart's expected.

Tom confesses to his family that he has invested in the Mermaid Boat Yard and his family is livid about the sale of the Flying Fish. Abby finds settling into the Tarrant social scene rather a challenge. Tom begins work at the Boat Yard where Avril remains coy about the buyer of his boat. Jan's mother, Kate, encourages her to accept Ken's offer of work. A distressed Abby takes some drastic action.

Leo acts like a hero. Jack has reservations about Tom's approach to the Mermaid Yard and Avril is caught in the crossfire. Abby's relationship with her mother continues to be a difficult one. Tom and Jan have a frank discussion about the state of their marriage when Jan finds herself preoccupied with her job at Ken Master's company.

Avril and Jack continue to disagree over the future of the Yard and Tom's role in the decision making. Jan offers Ken some business advice over dinner, much to Tom's annoyance. Leo takes a shine to Avril but Abby feels left out in the cold. Kate rescues Jack from a ditch and they have a heart to heart about business and family matters. Lynne and Tom sail the Flying Fish for one last time.

Abby secretly leaves for Southamptom leaving all in Tarrant mystified. Lynne is perturbed by Phil Norton's agenda and blows her chance of crewing for him. Charles Frere shows an interest in developing the marina. Ken uses his knowledge of who really bought the Flying Fish to drive Tom and Jan further apart.

Over dinner with Tom, Avril confesses to buying the Flying Fish. Polly encounters Charles at a gallery opening but does not get the reception she desires. She later admits to Jan that Gerald is not Abby's father. Ken continues to cause friction between Tom and Jan. Charles expresses an interest in purchasing the Mermaid Yard and saving it from financial ruin.

Charles and Ken come to gentleman's agreement about the planned marina. Jack turns to drink when the yard loses the German business contract and the bank threatens to foreclose on on the loan. Charles talks with Avril about purchasing the yard. When Tom wants to re-mortgage their home, Jan turns him down flat. Meanwhile, Ken offers Jan a helping hand and Leo finds Abby.

Charles enlists Gerald's help in his plans to develop the marina. Tom and Jan come to a financial agreement even though their marriage is over. Leo is determined to help Abby and her unborn baby. A mysterious man, Richard Shellet, claims to have a genuine claim over the Mermaid Yard. Jan travels to London where she meets fashion photographer Claude Dupont.

Tom and Avril's first night together is interrupted by a boating accident. When it emerges that the boat was recently serviced by the Mermaid Yard, there are criminal charges to answer. Leo becomes suspicious of his father's relationship with Avril. Jan is angered when Ken tells her what has been going on.

The legal battle between Jack and Skellet over the Mermaid Yard hots up. Tom adapts his boat designs to appease Jack while Charles and Ken's plans for the marina development forge ahead. Charles seduces Lynne and learns of Tom and Avril's affair. Jan receives a business offer from Claude Dupont and a personal offer from Ken. Kate invests in a racehorse.

There is descent at the Boat Yard because Tom, Avril and Jack are all too preoccupied elsewhere. Jan and Ken celebrate the opening of their new business venture, the Periplus Boutiquie. Shellet is happy to receive payment from Charles as they await the outcome of the legal action. Tom and Avril get support over his latest design from Relton.

Relton Marine is apprehensive about investing in the Boat Yard's latest project. Lynne's altered behaviour causes Tom and Jan some concern. As Charles waits for his American wife to arrive, news of his past relationship with Polly becomes public knowldge. Abby gives birth but her relationship with her own mother continues to be problematic.

Tom's new boat, Barracuda, is a financial success. The Shellet / Rolf trial draws to a close. When Lynne fails to return home, Jan is very concerned. Meanwhile, Ken offers her a shoulder to cry on. Tom searches for Lynne and holds Charles responsible for her disappearance. Avril is frustrated by Tom's obsession with finding Lynne.

Lynne lies unconscious in hospital. An impoverished Shellet looks to Charles for financial support following the collapse of the trial. Both Jan and Tom have difficulty concentrating on work. meanwhile, Charles encounters problems in obtaining his divorce. Kate and Jack have a major win on the horses. Gerald takes an instant dislike to Orin. A newspaper article could spell disaster for Periplus.

Ken and Charles continue with their ambitious plans for the marina development; however, they encounter local opposition when it emerges it will take place on a wildlife reserve. Abby and Orin try to agree over William's future. Ken asks Jan to marry him. In a last ditch attempt to help Lynne recover, Tom takes her out for a trip in the Flying Fish.

Charles persuades Avril to become Managing Director of Relton Marine. Shellet plans an explosive revenge and Jack receives a nasty blow. Abby is put under parental pressure to marry Orin. Because of Jack's injuries, he is unable to make his solo trip across the Atlantic in the Barracuda. Lynne takes up a new challenge without the knowledge of her parents.

Tom and Jan wait anxiously for news of Lynne. Charles secretly buys enough shares to gain full managerial control of Relton Marine. Local opposition to the marina development intensifies as Abby leads the protest. Ken attempts to bribe the council. Jack finally persuades Shellet to leave Tarrant for good. Following a storm at sea, Lynne loses radio contact and Tom and Jan are frantic.

Charles tries to distance himself from Ken Masters. Abby begins to neglect William because of her participation in the protest and social services are not happy. When the press takes an interest in the protest and the marine development, it appears that Ken's corruption may be exposed. Tom and Jan are relieved when Lynne finally makes radio contact.

Leo is up in court on criminal charges and is more than happy to expose Ken's corruption. However, Ken is eager to avoid a public trial at all costs. Charles and Ken continue to disagree about the direction of the marina project. Jan has second thought about her relationship with Ken when she learns the truth about Leo' s injuries.

Lynne revels in the glory of her boating success while her relationship with Claude Dupont flourishes.There are problems with The Lynnette taken out for a test voyage. Ken is introduced to business man Mark Foster. Avril expresses concern about possible takeover at Relton; she believes Gerald is behind it. Meanwhile, Gerald is humiliated when he learns the identity of Abby's father.

Tom experiences structural problems when he takes The Lynnette out for a trial. Ken expresses an interest in buying Fostercarf. Kate begins work at Periplus and she proves to be a very effective sales woman. Abby regrets giving William to Orin. Gerald gets his old job back. Charles is keen to get to know more about his daughter but Polly is not so happy.

Jack is in high sprits constructing his latest commision. Animal activist, Jaegar, encourages Abby to join in some dubious activities. Avril is concerned that Charles is going to take over Relton. Jan faces difficulty getting supplies when Claude's ex-girlfriend enacts revenge. Kate Harvey finds herself in dire financial trouble and her house may be at risk as result.

Curtis Jaegar takes drastic action to break up a dog fight and Abby tends his wounds. Charles continues with his mission to take over Relton. The Fosters and Ken celebrate their business merger. Meanwhile, Jan continues to experience difficulties at work and she, along with her mother, have serious financial worries. The Travis' express and interest in purchasing The Lynnette.

Charles announces to the press his impending takeover of Relton. Jack spends his time avoiding an admirer. Kate is forced to put her home up for sale as she falls deeper into debt. At the Mermaid, Hans Muller expresses an interest in the Barracuda and the Travis' take him out in The Lynnette. Jack refuses to attend a board meeting at Relton chaired by Charles. Disaster strikes The Lynnette

Following Mr. Travis' death on The Lynnette, the Yard and Tom are held accountable. They must prove it was caused by an accident, not a structural fault. Abby continues her involvement with Jaegar but is horrified when she discovers the true nature of his activist activities.

Sir Edward Frere arrives and expresses an interest in his son's business affairs. Jan finds herself in demand but when she is unable to keep up with requests for her clothes she decides to employ a new designer. Meanwhile, Kate settles into Jan's home. Following the catamaran incident, the Mermaid Yard struggles to find new contracts and negative publicity does little to alleviate their troubles.

Tom and Jack await the coroner's verdict and the Mermaid Yard continues to face financial difficulty. To add to their problems, Charles plans to withdraw the Barracuda from the market. Amanda pursues Leo but her outrageous actions create a stir. Robert McIntyre expresses an interest in Leisure Cruise but not everyone is eager to accept his potential investment.

McIntyre agrees to invest in Leisure Cruise but Mark Foster is definitely not happy. Leo's boat refurbishment business is a success and his first commission is from Amanda. Jan has trouble persuading Anna's traditional Chinese father the Anna should be given her independence.

The catamaran accident creates a heated debate at Relton. Meanwhile at the Mermaid Yard, workers are laid off. Mark Foster is determined to enter the Summer Powerboat race but this only leads to more conflict with Ken. Ken is eager for Leisure Cruise to beat Charles' boat in the race.

Leo's new business receives a boost when Amanda decides to invest. Ken and Sarah separate but Mark cannot cope with his wife's betrayal. When Avril is put in charge of renting out the units on the business park, there is an awkward meeting between her and Jan. Tom gets evidence that confirms the Travis' had an accident prior to the drowning incident.

Following the death of her husband, Sarah rejects Ken and contemplates taking her investment elsewhere. Jack pressurises Avril into asking Charles for money when the bank threatens to repossess the yard. Meanwhile, Emma finds more evidence that the Lynnette had been involved in a previous accident; however, she and Tom struggle to locate the incriminating evidence.

Jan's involvement in the Mermaid Yard continues to infuriate Jack. Leo begins working for Ken at Leisure Cruise. Anna is unhappy with her arranged marriage and, when she disappears, Jan is worried about the impact on the business. Gerald withdraws a substantial amount of money from his and Polly's bank account. He then disappears again.

When Avril wants the Barracuda put back on the market, Charles threatens to fire her if she goes ahead. While his business expands, his disagreements with Sarah intensify. Gerald explains his recent absences to Polly. There is a heated debate at the Mermaid Yard when they discuss a possible commission for Ken. Jan tells Sir Edward about Anna's disappearance and asks him for some business advice.

An old flame of Jack's, Vanessa, arrives and he misses the start of the Wolf Rock Race. Anna reveals the true extent of her family problems to Jan. Gerald is surprised to receive financial support from Charles and is even more surprised when Sir Edward offers him a job. Power boat racer Richard Spencer talks with Avril about joining Relton.

Tom's recent boating success is celebrated and the Baracuda is officially launched by Relton. Charles is disturbed to learn that his new business partner is his father. When Anna refuses to marry, her father denounces her. Polly decides to seek employment. David Lloyd warns Ken to keep an eye on Leisure Cruise. Jan is not impressed by the pace of work at the boat yard.

Leo and Amanda continue to argue and Polly throws herself into her work at Periplus. Sarah is angry at Ken for making business decisions without her knowledge. Avril sets out to resolve the conflict between the Mermaid Yard and Relton once and for all. Charles and Sir Edward hold a press conference to announce their joint business park venture.

Polly is left in charge of Periplus and the power goes to her head. Gerald is convinced that Sir Edward is out to ruin Ken. When a cheque from Ken is rejected by the bank, Avril and Tom are less enthusiastic about his latest commission at the boat yard. Leo and Amanda discuss her affair.

Ken and Sir Edward discuss the impending floatation of Leisure Cruise. Amanda's father accuses Leo of marrying his daughter for her money. Charles' new investors visit the business park and Jan's latest fashion designs prove popular with the critics. The yard's latest boat, The Spirit of Tarrant, is a great success.

Charles' and Avril's lives hang in the balance as they lie in intensive care. Meanwhile, Sir Edward, Jan and Jack fly out to Ireland to be by their side. When an old boyfriend of Emma's appears on the scene, Tom struggles to suppress his jealousy. Because of the accident, Relton share prices begin to fall and Ken is more than eager to cash in, much to Sarah's disgust.

Jan struggles to keep the theft of Anna's design plates under wraps, especially as Antonia puts her under pressure to come up with the goods. Amanda's father and Leo discuss the finer points of the divorce. Charles holds a press conference and is determined to spend more time with Avril and Abby. Sir Edward involves Tom and the Mermaid Yard with designs for the America's Cup.

Charles is disturbed to learn that Avril has discharged herself from the clinic and even more worried about her state of mind when she arrives for work as if nothing has happened. Sir Edward enrages Jan when he formally announces their engagement without her permission. Because of the Mermaid's involvement with the America's Cup, security is stepped up at the yard.

Sir Edward searches for oil with a total disregard for the bird sanctuary. Meanwhile, Ken has his own entrepreneurial ideas. Tom and Emma continue with their America's Cup design. Jan and Polly discuss business matters and Jan is resolute that she does not want to sell. In order to prevent Abby's custody battle being compromised, Sir Edward interferes with her relationship with Leo.

Ken learns of Sarah's duplicity and tries his hand at blackmail. He is also devastated to learn of Sir Edward's real business motivations. There is tension between Gerald and Avril but a nonchalant Charles refuses to become involved. Jan is befriended by fashion executive John Soames but their business relationship does not run smoothly.

Sir Edward does some grovelling and provides Tom with some inside information about the America's Cup. Meanwhile, when Jan runs out of stock, Sir Edward lends her a hand. Ken and Sarah's business relationship becomes more acrimonious when there is a press leak. Charles and Avril debate Sarah's loyalty. Some of Anna's stolen designs turn up in an unexpected place.

It's a race against time to save Jack's life. Ken's dubious past means that he has to rely on Sarah to secure the Langrcrest deal he's after. Jan is determined to find out who stole Anna's designs and Leo and Ken help her out. Charles involves Tom in his plans to create a new, international boat race. Avril and Charles doubt Gerald's business acumen. The Mermaid has a glut of horsepower engines.

Leo pressurises Ken into allowing him to race for Leisure Cruise in the world championships, and Ken agrees but only with the condition that Parker supports him. Meanwhile, Sarah reveals some business secrets to Charles. Polly continues in her entrepreneurial business venture without Jan's say.

Jan's concerns for Polly's plans to go into direct competition cause further disquiet. There are problems when Emma takes the Orkadian for a trial run without Jack's knowledge. Abby is eager for her photographic exhibition to be a critical success while Tom and Emma accept an appealing business proposition from Charles.

Ken is secretly pleased when Mike uncovers some secrets from Sir John Steven's past. Gerald attempts to suppress the conflict between Charles and Avril over the Langcrest deal. Under the guise of impressing Robert Hudson, Sir Edward convinces Jan to pose as his future wife. Meanwhile, Charles gives Abbie support when she raises concerns that her grandfather is manipulating her.

Robert Hudson arrives in Tarrant to discuss custody of William. When Polly supports Robert in apportioning blame on Abby, Gerald is livid with her. Charles is worried about Sarah's shares in Leisurecruise and things come to a head when he has dinner with Avril. Later, when Charles demands that Sarah be dismissed, Avril threatens to resign. Jack and Tom have a fracas at the Mermaid Yard.

Tom and Jack do some male bonding whilst out fishing. Polly is concerned to learn that Gerald has been cashing cheques from their account; they are virtually bankrupt. However, he will not reveal where the money has gone. Later, much to Polly's delight, they have reason to celebrate. Charles blames Avril for Tom's latest independent business venture.

Leo's racing ambition comes to a drastic halt while Ken celebrates a success. Sir Edward gives Tom a business offer he can't refuse. Charles is desperate to puchase a golf course from under his father's nose. There is a mystery buyer of Charles' recently released Relton Marine shares.

Leo begins to recover and Abby is there to help. Charles is concerned about being investigated by the fraud squad and Avril questions Gerald about what's going on. Meanwhile, in Polly's absence, Gerald and Abby share their concerns about the impending fraud trial. Jan wants to expand her business but doesn't want advice from Ken.

Jack tries to convince Tom that breaking up with Emma is not such a terrible thing. Charles prepares his legal team in order to avoid a fraud prosecution. Ken asks Tom to design a boat for Leisurecruise. When Charles and Gerald are cleared of all charges, the fraud squad are unhappy with Ken for supplying inaccurate information. Jan meets James Brooke, her potential competitor.

Gerald is perturbed to discover the Fraud Squad is still trailing him. Jack finds Vanessa easy to talk to and he confides his daughter's problems in her. Jan and James forge ahead in their new business venture HowardBrooke. Laura is keen to join forces with Ken but Tom is more reticent. With the fraud trial out of the way, Charles focuses all his attentions on removing Avril from Relton.

Jack and Avril go with Laura to Jimmy's funeral. Polly attempts to convince Abby to go to the States however Abby has other ideas. In an effort to reconcile Abby and Orin, Polly organises for him to visit. When Orin arrives it is evident he has come on business as well as personal matters. James and Jan are at loggerheads. Ken and Laura officially go into partnership.

Charles is concerned his father and the Hudson's might attempt a take over bid for Frere Holdings. Laura warns Ken to keep personal matters out of business. Meanwhile he is suspicious when numerous Leisurecruise shares are purchased by a mystery buyer. Leo's jealousy reaches boiling point when Polly attempts to reconcile Abby and Orin.

Jan and James disagree over designs and the direction of the firm. However later they get close up and personal. Jack is annoyed with Vanessa when he learns about her secret business dealings. Leo is taken in for questioning by the police. Meanwhile Tom is suspicious when Charles manages to get hold of a copy of his father's plans for the America's Cup.

Vanessa is given a new job but Tom is not convinced she's the right person for the job. Gerald learns to cope without Polly. Avril focuses her attention on preventing Charles' take over bid. Orin confesses he framed Leo. Charles is overjoyed at the idea of becoming a grandfather. Ken informs the fraud squad of Charles' dubious activities.

Charles is raided by the fraud squad and Ken tries to hide his guilt. Meanwhile, Kate is fully aware of his wrong doings and is determined to have him exposed. The order books are full at the Mermaid Yard and Tom and Jack have trouble completing work on time. Jan is busy making the HowardBrooke fashion show a success but James is preoccupied with Jan's previous relationship with Sir Edward.

Avril's business meeting in Malta does not go to plan when Sabio Fernandez delays his decision and she is requested to return to the UK to give evidence in the Charles Frere fraud case. Charles is determined that Avril should be made to look responsible. Meanwhile, Tom lends Avril a shoulder to cry on. Laura bribes James in order to get hold of his HowardBrooke shares.

Jan is livid with Ken for obtaining HowardBrooke shares by using blackmail. She is determined to stand by James, whatever the consequences. Charles' trial begins and Jack is convinced Avril harbours feelings for Charles. Meanwhile, she is still experiencing difficulty closing the Fernandez deal.

Charles and Gerald celebrate their innocent verdict and set their sights on revenge. Jack has trouble coming to terms with his feelings for Vanessa. Kate is determined to stop the marina development. Abby tells Charles that she is not going to hand William over to the Hudson's and that she's prepared to go to court to prevent it from happening.

Charles wins a boat race while Gerald tries to prevent any further decline in the price of Frere Holdings shares. Kate organises a formal protest against the marina development. However, Jack continues to contemplate selling out to Charles and comes to a decision about his life. Abby joins in but is forced to go home after she feels the baby move.

Avril is concerned about a take over bid when she learns that Ken has sold Charles his shares. Following his overdose, James' life hangs in the balance. Later, he gets revenge on Ken. Charles formalises his plans for the marina development. Leo angers Avril when he challenges Ken to a powerboat race. Meanwhile, Avril is also livid with her father for contemplating the sale of the yard.

Leo and Abby christen their son Thomas Leo in honour of Leo's father, who died three weeks previously. Jack, who is struggling to come to terms with Tom's death, needs some time on his own. Whilst the Howard family countinues to mourn Tom, Charles relishes his new role as grandfather.

Ken and Avril's business relationship is in jeopardy when it emerges Laura has a controlling share of Leisurecruise. Charles, still adamant he will out do Avril, decides to manipulate Ken in order to gain ownership of the Mermaid, and Relton. Meanwhile, Ken is busy trying to encourage Jan to accept his offer of investment as she expands her business in Gibraltar.

Sir Edward Frere returns and is prepared to support Jan's business proposition to expand into the perfume industry. Leo, Bill and Jack prepare for their journey on the Xanada, despite everyone's concerns. Vanessa is angry about Jack's foolish behaviour and Abby is annoyed with Leo and accuses him of not supporting her. Orin is employed at Leisurecruise by Laura.

Orin re-organises Leisurecruise and discusses the possibility of a Relton takeover bid with Laura. The Xanadu returns with Lynne on board. Charles' suspicions are aroused when a new Frere Holdings-Leisurecruise alliance is suggested. However, he continues to struggle with his marina project. Ken blackmails Sir Edward to secure the financial support he needs to gain ownership of Leisurecruise.

Sir Edward's health declines and Jan learns that he has rejected all medical intervention. Avril is concerned that the Mermaid cannot fulfil its orders and is at logger heads with Orin over the slow completion of the Leisurecruise commission; however, Laura is overjoyed at the delays in production. Jan is angry when Sir Edward implies she must regret not marrying him when she had the chance.

It's Sir Edward's funeral but Polly doesn't attend, neither does Charles who is unexpectedly shaken by his father's death. Venessa reveals that the mysterious new arrival in Tarrant is her brother, David Relton. When Sir John retires from the bank many believe his nephew has had a hand in his departure. Orin offers Leo money in a bid to win back Abby. Lynne launches her range of cosmetics.

Charles assures the press that his father's death has not had a negative impact on Frere Holdings, but share prices continue to fall. Abby's turmoil continues following the reading of Sir Edward's will; she is uncertain about how to continue her relationship with Leo and still maintain contact with William.

When Relton doesn't return from Malta, Laura, Ken and Avril realise the mistake they made doing business with him. Charles has trouble convincing Abby it's in her best interest to allow him to contest his father's will. Meanwhile, Abby begins to enjoy spending her inheritance. Later, Charles approaches Leo and offers to act on his behalf to avoid losing Thomas.

Leo and Abby go their separate ways. Ken is overjoyed to learn that Relton has duped both Laura and Avril. Jan and Charles have a heated row about his involvement with Leo and Abby. Charles also finds himself at odds with Gerald. Laura wants compensation for her losses from Avril. Gerald agrees to leave Charles to work for Relton Marine, and Avril.

Vanessa apologises to Avril for her brother's behaviour. When news of the fraud hits the press, Avril is implicated; it seems Charles may be behind the leak. Avril is convinced it is to blacken her name and have her removed from the Relton board. Admiral Redfern is announced as the new bank chairman and he is happy to support Jan's business.

The Mermaid continues to struggle to complete its orders on time. Ken offers Pierre a role on the Poelma Corporation board while Avril speculates how Ken obtained the majority share. Robert begins to manage Charels' financial affairs. Jack reveals his potential paternity suit to Vanessa, only to learn that Bill too may also be Tony's father. The Frere Five Star Cup is a closely fought contest.

Ken blackmails Laura into selling her ever increasing number of shares in the House of Howard to him. In Bermuda, Gerald supports Orin in his confrontation with Charles over William. Jan requests Admiral Redfern's support in obtaining such much needed funding. Laura requests support from Avril in a move against Ken and his growing business interests.

Abby tells Charles he has been usurped as Chairman of Frere Holdings and admits she backed the move. Jack finally decides to leave the Mermaid; he wants Leo to take over. Lynne returns from Bermuda in time to help launch the new cosmetics range. Pierre reveals to Avril that he too backed the move to oust Charles in an act of revenge; his father was once cheated by him.
